key_insight: SrTiO3−xHx oxyhydrides strongly favor a cis O4H2 anion arrangement, and this ordering is highly sensitive to the DFT+U choice, with U = 3.3 eV matching HSE06-like energetics.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite oxyhydride design, accurate anion-order predictions require calibrated electronic-structure settings, because the wrong U value can misrank stable configurations by ~100 meV/anion.
method: Built a cluster expansion for SrTiO3−xHx using HSE06-informed energetics.
Compared DFT+U mixing/order energies across U values to identify an HSE06 proxy.
Used CE ground states and Monte Carlo sampling to map anion-order preferences.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to ~100 meV/anion sensitivity to DFT+U and a ~200 meV per hydride stabilization for the cis O4H2 configuration, supported by benchmark HSE06 calculations and CE/MC sampling.
watch_item: Because ordering energetics are strongly U-dependent, CE models trained with an unvalidated DFT+U setting may give misleading phase stability and local-order predictions.
paper_title: Long- and Short-Range Anion Order in SrTiO$_{3-x}$H$_x$ Perovskite Oxyhydrides: DFT+$U$ Sensitivity and HSE06 Cluster Expansion
